narrative.overview:
Transit Education's design system is built around one truth: the students who walk in are making a life-changing decision, often for the first time, and they need to feel both inspired and safe. The system is warm but expert — like a knowledgeable friend who has navigated this journey before and walks beside you through every step.

Crimson Passport Red is the system's authority signal. It appears purposefully — on headings, interactive elements, and navigation — never as decoration. White space does the heavy lifting; the palette is deliberately restrained so that when red appears, it carries full weight.

Typography is set in Poppins — a geometric humanist sans with warmth in the curves and authority in the weight. Headlines are tight, bold, and confident. Body copy breathes at 1.7 line height, comfortable for first-language-Nepali readers working through information-dense destination guides.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained crimson authority — one primary accent, used with intent
Warm white canvas — off-white backgrounds, not stark white, for approachability
Confident Poppins type — tight letter-spacing on headlines, comfortable body leading
Choreographed motion — slide-up and fade transitions; never gratuitous
Premium proportions — generous padding, refined radius scale, polished hover states

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Passport Red is the only accent. It appears on ≤15% of any given screen. Its rarity is what makes it feel like authority rather than noise.

rules.name: The Warm Temperature Rule
rules.body: Every neutral pulls slightly warm. #F3F3F1 not #F3F3F3. #111111 not #000000. The system should feel approachable, not sterile.

rules.name: The No-Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Button and navigation labels are sentence case or title case, never ALL-CAPS. This brand's authority comes from weight and color, not case.

rules.name: The Heading Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings use weight (700–800) for hierarchy, not size alone. Don't compensate for weak hierarchy by inflating font sizes.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces carry no shadow by default. Shadow appears only on hover or when structural separation is required. A shadow on a resting card is visual noise.

dos: Do use Passport Red only on interactive and authority elements — keep it rare (≤15% screen coverage)
Do use Warm Canvas (#FAFAF8) as the default page background instead of Pure White
Do set body copy at 1.7 line-height minimum for comfortable reading
Do use the full radius scale: 10px for controls, 14–18px for cards, 22–26px for featured cards
Do keep button and nav labels in sentence case or title case — never ALL-CAPS
Do apply Ambient Lift shadow only on hover — cards should be flat at rest
Do cite real specifics in copy: visa approval rates, partner universities, destination names
donts: Don't use generic ed-tech stock photography (students jumping, pointing at laptops, posed with globes)
Don't introduce rainbow or multi-accent color schemes — Passport Red is the only accent
Don't use cluttered information grids, dense feature walls, or form-like layouts
Don't use ALL-CAPS for buttons, navigation, or headings
Don't stack shadows — flat at rest, one lift on hover only
Don't use Alert Red (#EF4444) decoratively — error states only
Don't use pure #000000 black or pure #FFFFFF white as backgrounds — the system runs warm
Don't add typefaces beyond Poppins and Geist Mono
